title: When Geometry Becomes an Engine
mathematical_role: Expose time-indexed metric evolution as a changing geometric world while keeping qualitative curvature concentration distinct from geometry itself.
learning_objective: Read g(t) as an evolving metric and retain a memorable picture of geometry as a dynamical object without mistaking the plate for a computed flow.
literal_semantics: The displayed evolution law is d g/dt = -2 Ric(g).
The upper sequence is ordered t0, t1, t2.
Curvature concentration is encoded separately from the displayed 3D surface geometry.
nonliteral_semantics: The rendered surfaces are synthetic teaching surfaces, not literal three-manifolds or numerical Ricci-flow states.
The lower curvature map uses a surface-Laplacian proxy solely to separate geometry from qualitative concentration.
Surface height, color, contour spacing, and the highlighted concentration are not canonical-neighbourhood or singularity data.

notes: Representation-repair realization follows independent rejection of the SVG-only candidate.

renderer.version_or_environment: requirements/visual-pedagogy-render.txt; deterministic Matplotlib/Numpy raster renderer v4
reproducibility_notes: No randomness or external service is used.
The committed PNG is reproduced byte-for-byte in the dedicated representation-repair workflow.
Rendering reproducibility does not establish any Ricci-flow analytic estimate or theorem.

derivatives.role: current high-resolution 3D/raster review candidate; not live documentary asset

accessibility.alt_text: Three rendered teaching surfaces show an ordered metric evolution from t0 to t2, followed by a separate qualitative curvature-concentration map.
accessibility.long_description: The plate separates geometric state from curvature encoding. Three synthetic 3D surfaces represent ordered metric states. A distinct lower heat map visualizes a qualitative concentration proxy, and the claim boundary states that neither element is a numerical Ricci-flow solution or singularity certificate.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Pedagogical reconstruction of metric evolution and separate qualitative curvature concentration.
not_claimed: A proof of Hamilton-Perelman estimates or the Poincare theorem

supersession_reason: Representation-layer repair replaces the rejected SVG realization with a deterministic high-resolution 3D/raster teaching plate while preserving the non-evidentiary boundary.
